newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar slumps as white premiums sold.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar slumps as white premiums sold.

text.p: White sugar futures extended their decline in solid Tuesday trade as a weak New York market drew out premium sellers and spot December staged another successive session of losses.
Trade and commission house sales kept nearby positions pinned down and the weaker New York open encouraged trade selling of the March/March premium.
"It didn't help a bit because premium sellers jumped all over it at $80...everything leads to pressure," said one trader.
At 1550 GMT December was down $5.90 at $326.50 and March down $5.90 at $326.50, leaving little room for manoeuvre on London's Dec/March spread.
Overall volume totalled 2,598 lots, dominated by the front two positions.
The steep falls in December's value set in on Friday, the session prior to December taking centre stage as spot position, but the overwhelming weakness was evident earlier in the week.
Last Monday December notched up an intraday high of $347.60, about $20 higher than current levels.
Technical analysts said the weak London market was due for an upside correction, given that values had moved into oversold territory.
"With the RSI (Relative Strength Index) now well into oversold levels, a correction to the upside or some form of consolidation can be expected," said Darren Gurner, a technical analyst at Sucden.
Paris positions also lost ground. December was down $6.30 and $326.60 and March was down $5.90 at $327.50. Matif volume was 884 lots.
